bottom_line: In patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction, mortality from all causes was significantly reduced with captopril vs placebo (reduction in risk 19 percent; 95 percent confidence interval, 3 to 32 percent; P = 0.019).
implications: These data support the conclusion that, in this trial population, captopril vs placebo was associated with lower all-cause mortality (275/1116 vs 228/1115; risk reduction 19%, 95% CI 3 to 32) and lower cardiovascular mortality (234 vs 188; risk reduction 21%, 95% CI 5 to 35). The document does not establish effects in patients outside the enrolled criteria (e.g., those with ejection fraction >40% or with overt heart failure requiring vasodilator therapy).
